thread:
Eli: quick PSA  had a major ISP blip during standup, tethered phone to laptop and limp-synced for 20min. anyone use a cheap USB ethernet adapter as a backup? looking for a last-minute gift for my home-office escape kit. :dizzy_face:
Noor: yes! I keep a $15 USB-C to ethernet in my drawer. lifesaver. make sure it's gigabit, avoid the super-cheap clones that drop to 100mbps.
Sam: also note: if you're on Mac, disable "automatic proxy discovery" when tethering; weird proxy settings can kill the link. learned the hard way. :face_with_head_bandage:
Priyanka: pro tip: Mac/Win both support USB tethering where you plug phone via USB and enable "USB tethering" in phone settings. way more stable than hotspot wifi.
Eli: great tips. any suggestions for stealth-cable runs if the router is in the hallway and you don't want to run a cable across the living room? roommate politics. :grimacing:
Gabe: flat ethernet under the door works and is reversible. use gaffer tape on the edges if concerned about trips. if it's one-off, buy a 30ft and loop it along baseboards.
Noor: if you need immediate next-day, check local office-supply stores for long patch cables. or ask ops-bot if office has spare adapters.
ops-bot: reminder: IT spare-parts locker has a small stash of USB ethernet adapters and patch cables. submit a ticket at https://internal/it/spares and choose "pickup". :package:
Sam: also toss a small travel router in your kit. helps create a small private AP off the wired line. plus you can use it as a repeater if the landlord router is weak.
Priyanka: cheap travel routers are surprisingly handy. I keep one with a tiny power brick and a patch cable in my "escape bag".
Eli: adding a travel router + USB ethernet adapter to cart now. will report back after I build the emergency kit and maybe a tiny soft-case to hold everything. photo reward offered. :camera_with_flash:
